---
description: "How complete and accurate Island Transit's live bus tracking is: trips seen, gaps, location age and prediction misses."
title: "Can the data be trusted?"
subtitle: "How reliable Island Transit's bus-tracking feed is, checked every day"
---

Trip-planning apps, this site, and anyone else who studies Island Transit
all lean on the same live feed, so every number built on it is only as good
as the feed itself. That's why we grade the feed every day.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
import {csv, json, pct, num, count, unit, routeLabel, longDate, pacificClock, plural, isFalse, isoDate, serviceDays, recentDays, withDates, showAllToggle, emptyNote, guard, stats, h, DATA_URL, DATA_RAW_URL} from "./lib.js"
import {makeCharts} from "./charts.js"
ch = makeCharts({Plot})
daily = csv(d3, "data/quality/daily.csv")
minutes = s => s == null ? null : s / 60
// Days with scheduled service; a holiday is archived and listed under "All
// days" but not graded or charted.
days = withDates(serviceDays(daily)).map(d => ({...d, prediction_min_5min: minutes(d.prediction_median_abs_s_5min)}))
latestDate = days.length ? days.at(-1).day : null
latest = latestDate ? json(`data/quality/days/${latestDate}.json`) : null
noData = () => days.length === 0 ? emptyNote("no-days") : emptyNote("unavailable", `The details for ${longDate(latestDate)}`)
ev = latest?.events ?? null
routeName = id => routeLabel(latest?.routes, id)
```

::: {.slot-stats}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  const lq = days.at(-1);
  if (lq == null) return noData();
  const partial = latest?.scheduled_service?.trips_ended_before_collection > 0 && latest?.paradata?.observed_from;
  const far = lq.prediction_over_30min_share_5min;
  return html`<p class="note">These grades are for ${longDate(latestDate)}.${partial ? ` Collection began at ${pacificClock(latest.paradata.observed_from)} Pacific that day, so the grades cover only part of it.` : ""}</p>
  ${stats([
    {label: "Did every scheduled trip show up?", value: pct(lq.trip_coverage),
     note: `of ${count(lq.scheduled_trips)} scheduled trips appeared in the tracking around the time they were due`},
    {label: "Did the collector keep running?", value: pct(lq.vehicle_uptime, 1),
     note: "of 20-second checks got a good answer from the feed"},
    {label: "How fresh are bus locations?", value: unit(lq.position_age_s_median, "second"),
     note: "typical age of a location when it first appears"},
    {label: "How close are arrival predictions?", value: unit(lq.prediction_min_5min, "min", 1, "min"),
     note: `typical miss, for predictions made 5 minutes before the bus arrived${far ? `; ${pct(far)} were off by more than 30 minutes` : ""}`},
    {label: "Are buses where the route says?", value: lq.off_shape_share == null ? "–" : pct(1 - lq.off_shape_share),
     note: "of locations were within 100 meters (about 330 feet) of the bus's published route"},
  ])}`;
}, "The day's grades")
```
:::

We sort the details below the way survey researchers grade any source of
data, into [coverage]{.term tip="Coverage asks whether every scheduled trip shows up in the tracking at all."},
[nonresponse]{.term tip="Nonresponse is data that should be there but is missing, such as a failed request, an empty feed, or a gap in a bus's reports."},
[measurement error]{.term tip="Measurement error is data that is there but wrong, such as GPS wobble, a bus that seems to jump, an old location, or a prediction that misses."},
[processing error]{.term tip="A processing error happens when data can't be matched up, such as a trip in the feed that isn't in the schedule."}
and [paradata]{.term tip="Paradata is data about the collection itself: every request the collector made, how long it took, and whether it worked."}.
Hover over or tap each term for a plain explanation, or see the
[Methods](methods.qmd) page for the exact definitions.

## Over time

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof showAll = showAllToggle(days.length)
```

::: {.slot-trends}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
series = [
  {key: "trip_coverage", title: "Scheduled trips seen in the feed", share: true},
  {key: "vehicle_uptime", title: "Collector uptime (vehicle locations)", share: true},
  {key: "stale_in_service_rate", title: "Feed more than 2 minutes behind during service", share: true},
  {key: "position_age_s_median", title: "Typical age of a bus location when first seen", word: "second"},
  {key: "longest_gap_s_median", title: "Typical longest tracking gap per trip", word: "second"},
  {key: "timepoint_coverage", title: "Departures at timetable stops we could time", share: true},
  {key: "prediction_min_5min", title: "Typical arrival prediction miss, 5 minutes ahead", word: "minute"},
]
guard(() => {
  if (days.length === 0) return noData();
  if (days.length < 2) return emptyNote("one-day", "Charts that follow each measure over time");
  const shown = recentDays(days, showAll);
  const say = (s, v) => s.share ? pct(v, 1) : unit(v, s.word, 1);
  return html`<div class="chart-grid">${series.map(s => ch.figure({
    title: s.title, value: say(s, days.at(-1)[s.key]),
    chart: ch.trend(shown, {
      y: s.key, share: !!s.share, height: 200, maxTicks: 5, yLabel: s.share ? null : `${s.word}s`,
      ariaLabel: `${s.title}, by service day`,
      describe: `From ${longDate(shown[0].day)} to ${longDate(latestDate)}. Latest value: ${say(s, days.at(-1)[s.key])}. Every day's value is in the table under "All days".`,
      tip: d => `${longDate(d.day)}\n${say(s, d[s.key])}`,
    }),
  }))}</div>`;
}, "The charts over time")
```
:::

## Details

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => latest == null ? noData() : html`<p>These details are for ${longDate(latestDate)}${latest.schedule?.passio_version
```

<details class="more"><summary>Trip coverage by route</summary>

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  const rows = Object.entries(latest?.coverage?.by_route ?? {}).map(([id, c]) => ({route: routeName(id), ...c}));
  if (rows.length === 0) return noData();
  return ch.figure({
    chart: ch.bars(rows, {
      category: "route", value: "coverage", axisLabel: "Share of scheduled trips seen",
      ariaLabel: `Share of scheduled trips seen in the tracking, by route, ${longDate(latestDate)}`,
      tip: d => `${d.route}\n${count(d.observed)} of ${count(d.scheduled)} trips (${pct(d.coverage)})`,
    }),
    table: ch.table(rows, {
      caption: `Scheduled trips seen in the tracking, by route, ${longDate(latestDate)}`,
      sort: {key: "coverage", descending: true}, pageSize: 40,
      columns: [
        {key: "route", label: "Route"},
        {key: "coverage", label: "Trips seen", align: "right", format: v => pct(v)},
        {key: "observed", label: "Seen", align: "right", format: count},
        {key: "scheduled", label: "Scheduled", align: "right", format: count},
      ],
    }),
  });
}, "Trip coverage by route")
```

</details>

<details class="more"><summary>Timepoint events observed, by route</summary>

This shows how many scheduled departures at printed timepoints (or arrivals,
at a trip's last stop) we could put a time on, using the bus locations.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  const rows = Object.entries(ev?.stop_coverage?.timepoints?.by_route ?? {}).map(([id, c]) => ({
    route: routeName(id), ...c, off_shape_share: ev?.shape_fit?.by_route?.[id]?.off_shape_share ?? null}));
  if (rows.length === 0) return noData();
  return ch.figure({
    chart: ch.bars(rows, {
      category: "route", value: "coverage", axisLabel: "Share of scheduled timepoint events observed",
      ariaLabel: `Share of scheduled timepoint events we could time, by route, ${longDate(latestDate)}`,
      tip: d => `${d.route}\n${count(d.observed)} of ${count(d.scheduled)} events (${pct(d.coverage)})\nPositions off the route shape: ${pct(d.off_shape_share, 1)}`,
    }),
    table: ch.table(rows, {
      caption: `Scheduled timepoint events we could time, by route, ${longDate(latestDate)}`,
      sort: {key: "coverage", descending: true}, pageSize: 40,
      columns: [
        {key: "route", label: "Route"},
        {key: "coverage", label: "Events timed", align: "right", format: v => pct(v)},
        {key: "observed", label: "Timed", align: "right", format: count},
        {key: "scheduled", label: "Scheduled", align: "right", format: count},
        {key: "off_shape_share", label: "Locations off route", align: "right", format: v => pct(v, 1)},
      ],
    }),
  });
}, "Timepoint events by route")
```

</details>

<details class="more"><summary>Arrival predictions</summary>

For each prediction, we take the arrival time the feed was showing a given
number of minutes ahead and subtract the arrival time we estimated from the
bus's locations. A positive error means the bus showed up earlier than the
feed said it would. Some predictions carry the wrong day's date, so we count
those separately and leave them out of the error figures. A few others are
off by hours, which pulls the mean far from the typical miss, so the table
gives both the mean and the median and counts the predictions that were off
by more than 30 minutes.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  const rows = Object.entries(ev?.prediction_error?.by_horizon_min ?? {}).map(([ahead, b]) => ({ahead: +ahead, ...b}));
  if (rows.length === 0) return noData();
  const seconds = v => num(v, 1);
  return ch.table(rows, {
    caption: `Arrival prediction error by minutes ahead, ${longDate(latestDate)}`, wide: true,
    columns: [
      {key: "ahead", label: "Minutes ahead", align: "right"},
      {key: "n", label: "Predictions", align: "right", format: count},
      {key: "bias_s", label: "Mean error (seconds)", align: "right", format: seconds},
      {key: "median_s", label: "Median error (seconds)", align: "right", format: seconds},
      {key: "median_abs_s", label: "Typical miss (seconds)", align: "right", format: seconds},
      {key: "mae_s", label: "Mean miss (seconds)", align: "right", format: seconds},
      {key: "within_60s_share", label: "Within 60 seconds", align: "right", format: v => pct(v, 1)},
      {key: "over_30min", label: "Off by over 30 minutes", align: "right", format: count},
      {key: "other_day", label: "Dated another day", align: "right", format: count},
    ],
  });
}, "The prediction figures")
```

</details>

<details class="more"><summary>Fields the feed leaves empty</summary>

This table shows how often each field is missing from the position reports.
When a field is missing from every single report, the feed simply doesn't
send it.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  const rows = Object.entries(latest?.nonresponse?.items?.missing_share ?? {}).map(([field, share]) => ({field, share}));
  if (rows.length === 0) return noData();
  return ch.table(rows, {
    caption: `Share of position reports missing each field, ${longDate(latestDate)}`, pageSize: 40,
    columns: [
      {key: "field", label: "Field", format: v => h("code", {}, v)},
      {key: "share", label: "Missing", align: "right", format: v => pct(v, 1)},
    ],
  });
}, "The table of empty fields")
```

<details class="more"><summary>Other figures for the day</summary>

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  if (latest == null) return noData();
  const q = latest, m = q.measurement ?? {}, fit = ev?.shape_fit ?? {};
  const refresh = q.paradata?.tripUpdates?.refresh;
  const canceled = q.coverage?.canceled_trips;
  const of = (a, b) => a == null || b == null ? "–" : `${count(a)} of ${count(b)}`;
  const rows = [
    ["Fetch failures, vehicle positions", pct(q.nonresponse?.fetch?.vehiclePositions?.rate, 2)],
    ["Empty vehicle feed while buses are scheduled", pct(q.nonresponse?.vehicle_feed?.empty_in_service_rate, 2)],
    ["Positions with no trip, an unknown trip, or a trip not scheduled that day", pct(q.coverage?.over_coverage?.share, 2)],
    ["Trips the feed marked as canceled", canceled == null ? "not measured for this day" : canceled === 0 ? "none" : count(canceled)],
    ["Impossible jumps (over 130 km/h, about 80 mph)", count(m.impossible_jumps_over_130_kmh)],
    ["Vehicle timestamps in the future", count(m.timestamps_in_future)],
    ["Vehicle timestamps going backwards", count(m.timestamps_going_backwards)],
    ["Trip ids found in the schedule", pct(q.processing?.id_match?.trip_id?.match_rate, 1)],
    ["Stop ids found in the schedule", pct(q.processing?.id_match?.stop_id?.match_rate, 1)],
    ["Median response time, vehicle positions", unit(q.paradata?.vehiclePositions?.latency_ms_median, "millisecond")],
    ...(refresh == null ? [] : [
      ["Checks 20 seconds apart in which a trip's prediction had changed", pct(refresh.changed_share, 1)],
      ["Typical time between new predictions for a trip", unit(refresh.update_interval_s_median, "second")],
    ]),
    ["Distinct vehicles reporting", count(q.coverage?.vehicles_seen)],
    ...(ev == null ? [] : [
      ["All stop events with an inferred time", pct(ev.stop_coverage?.all_stops?.coverage, 1)],
      ["Positions more than 100 meters (about 330 feet) off the route shape", pct(fit.off_shape_share, 1)],
      ["Positions moving against the route shape", pct(fit.wrong_direction_share, 1)],
      ["Trips that left out part of the published route shape", fit.trips_skipping_part_of_shape == null ? "–"
        : `${count(fit.trips_skipping_part_of_shape)} (${num(fit.skipped_km, 1)} km, about ${num(fit.skipped_km * 0.621371, 1)} miles)`],
      ["Route shapes that draw segments three times (corrected)", of(ev.retraced_shapes?.shapes_retraced, ev.retraced_shapes?.shapes_used)],
      ["Trip ids seen that are not scheduled that day", of(ev.assignment?.unassignable, ev.assignment?.observed_trip_ids)],
      ["Position jitter at terminals, 95th percentile", ev.jitter?.jitter_m_p95 == null ? "–"
        : `${num(ev.jitter.jitter_m_p95, 1)} meters (about ${num(ev.jitter.jitter_m_p95 * 3.28084)} feet)`],
      ["Vehicles seen in the previous 30 days but not this day",
        ev.missing_vehicles == null ? "–" : ev.missing_vehicles.missing_count == null ? "no earlier days" : count(ev.missing_vehicles.missing_count)],
    ]),
  ].map(([measure, value]) => ({measure, value}));
  return ch.table(rows, {
    caption: `Other quality figures for ${longDate(latestDate)}`, pageSize: 40,
    columns: [{key: "measure", label: "Measure", sortable: false}, {key: "value", label: "Value", align: "right", sortable: false}],
  });
}, "The day's other figures")
```

</details>

<details class="more"><summary>Randomness of gaps</summary>

When the feed misses a trip, is that bad luck spread evenly, or does it
tend to happen at certain hours, on certain routes, or when lots of buses
are out at once? The tables below show the share of scheduled trips that
sent no position report around the time they were due, over every day so
far. Once there are enough days and enough missed trips, a statistical model
called a logistic regression will test all of these at the same time.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
gaps = json("data/quality/gaps.json")
pval = p => p == null ? "–" : p < 0.0001 ? "< 0.0001" : `= ${num(p, 4)}`
guard(() => {
  const rates = gaps?.rates;
  if (rates == null || Object.keys(rates).length === 0) return noData();
  const named = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(rates.by_route ?? {}).map(([id, v]) => [routeName(id), v]));
  const groups = [
    ["Hour band (Pacific)", rates.by_hour_band, false],
    ["Trips in service at the trip's start", rates.by_trips_in_service, false],
    ["Day type", rates.by_day_type, false],
    ["Route", named, true],
  ].filter(([, t]) => t && Object.keys(t).length);
  return html`
    <p>Over ${plural(gaps.days?.length ?? 0, "day")}, ${count(gaps.trips)} trips were scheduled and
      ${count(gaps.unobserved)} sent no position report within 30 minutes of their scheduled time.</p>
    <div class="chart-grid">${groups.map(([title, t, sortable]) => html`<div>
      <h3 class="chart-title">${title}</h3>
      ${ch.table(Object.entries(t).map(([group, v]) => ({group, ...v})), {
        caption: `Scheduled trips not seen, by ${title.toLowerCase()}`, pageSize: 40,
        columns: [
          {key: "group", label: "Group", sortable},
          {key: "scheduled", label: "Scheduled", align: "right", format: count, sortable},
          {key: "unobserved", label: "Not seen", align: "right", format: count, sortable},
          {key: "rate", label: "Share not seen", align: "right", format: v => pct(v, 1), sortable},
        ],
      })}</div>`)}</div>`;
}, "The gap tables")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  if (gaps == null) return html``;
  const model = gaps.model;
  if (model == null) {
    const status = gaps.model_status ?? "";
    return status === "" ? html`` : html`<p><em>${status.startsWith("not fitted: needs")
      ? `The model hasn't been fitted yet, because it ${status.slice("not fitted: ".length)}.`
      : `Model status: ${status}.`}</em></p>`;
  }
  // The file named these with spaces at first and with underscores since.
  const ref = model.reference_levels ?? {};
  const level = key => ref[key] ?? ref[key.replace("_", " ")];
  const test = model.lr_test_all_predictors ?? {};
  const terms = (model.terms ?? []).filter(t => t.term !== "intercept").map(t => ({...t,
    term: t.term.startsWith("route: ") ? `route: ${routeName(t.term.slice(7))}` : t.term.replaceAll("_", " "),
    low: t.or_95ci?.[0], high: t.or_95ci?.[1]}));
  return html`
  <p>This logistic regression looks at ${count(model.trips)} trips and asks which ones the feed missed. We fit it with
  Firth's penalized likelihood, which keeps the estimates sensible even when a route never missed a trip.
  Testing all the predictors together gives χ² = ${num(test.statistic, 1)},
  df = ${count(test.df)}, p ${pval(test.p)}.
  A small p-value means the gaps are not missing completely at random, so something about the hour, the route,
  the day or the number of buses out is tied to which trips go missing. The model treats every trip as
  separate, but trips lost on the same day or the same bus tend to go missing together, so the p-values
  here are more confident than they should be. Each odds ratio compares a group with
  ${level("hour_band")}, route ${routeName(level("route"))}
  and ${level("day_type")}.${model.converged ? "" : " The model did not settle on a stable answer (it did not converge), so treat these numbers with caution."}</p>
  ${ch.table(terms, {
    caption: "Odds ratios from the model of which trips the feed missed", pageSize: 40,
    columns: [
      {key: "term", label: "Term"},
      {key: "odds_ratio", label: "Odds ratio", align: "right", format: v => num(v, 2)},
      {key: "low", label: "95% interval, low", align: "right", format: v => num(v, 2)},
      {key: "high", label: "95% interval, high", align: "right", format: v => num(v, 2)},
      {key: "p", label: "p", align: "right", format: v => pval(v).replace(/^= /, "")},
    ],
  })}`;
}, "The model of gaps")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<p>The model and the data behind it are in
<a href="${DATA_RAW_URL}/quality/gaps.json"><code>quality/gaps.json</code></a>.
Holidays on which Island Transit runs no buses are left out.</p>`
```
